title: Hubble: Decagon Around Saturn's South Pole
explanation:
# Saturn's Mysterious Geometric Poles

Saturn's north and south poles are crowned with strikingly different geometric cloud formations—a stable six-sided hexagon discovered in 1987 and a newly observed ten-sided decagon—likely sculpted by the collision of fast-moving atmospheric winds from the equator crashing into slower polar winds, creating these mathematical boundaries in the swirling clouds. While the hexagon has remained rock-solid for over four decades, astronomers are still puzzled by whether this newfound decagon will prove equally persistent, making Saturn's poles a fascinating natural laboratory for understanding how planetary atmospheres organize themselves into such precise shapes.
